# III. FOOTSTEPS [italic]Entry three. Day 211. I said I would write every three days. I was busy being afraid.[/italic]
The Union does not send men with guns for someone like me. I am not worth a ship. It sends patience. The Ministry of Space Security has people on Union worlds, on American worlds, inside the corporations. A rifleman from a hab stack is a thin file. Thin files are not closed. They wait.
## THINGS I NOTICED THIS WEEK - A new man at the canteen who hums while he eats. I knew the tune before he reached the chorus. Then he stopped, as if he had remembered something. - My locker at the works was opened and closed again. Nothing was taken. That is worse. - The embassy page says the reports of a Ministry office on this colony are false. I had heard no reports. I heard the denial.
I have other fears that do not speak Russian. The garrison would like me very much. A Union deserter is something to write up and send up the chain. They would not hand me back, not at first. They would keep me in a room and ask about the ship, the rifles, the name of our officer, until I had nothing left. Then they would trade me anyway, when the talks needed a gift.
The marshal thinks I am a pipe fitter with the name on the coverall. Let him.
I sleep with my boots on, like on the ship. My bag is under the bed: two days of food, a knife, a filter mask, the papers I bought. I filed the number off my identity disc and dropped it down a drain shaft, and the next night I went back to make sure it was still gone.
If somebody knocks at night, I will not open. If I stop writing, it was not my choice. Look for me on [netlink="missing.deep" link="missing.deep"].
[color=#5A5040]-- still here. still here. still[/color]
